content:
erin: Heads-up — after the kernel-path-selection rollout (hybrid-attn + quant-fallback) on staging->prod this morning, /rt-gen is showing a sustained prefix cache hit-rate collapse on warm starts. Quick numbers: prefix hit-rate was ~62% baseline, dropped to ~14% after rollout; 95p latency +18%, token cost +12%. Rolling back the kernel variant returns hit-rate to ~60%. Need triage.

jia: Ugh. Do we have a profiler dump or flamegraph? Any visible change in key generation or normalization stage?

erin: Uploaded a quick trace to perf-bot, and pasted the tiny log excerpt below. It looks like many KV lookups are returning key_mismatch instead of miss due to hash differences, not just eviction.

sam: Can you drop the log snippet and the kernel flags used for the rollout? Also which quant profile?

erin: Kernel flags from the deploy: 
```
--kernel-path=hybrid_vectorized
--attn-opt=tiling_v2
--quant-profile=aq8_dynamic
--kv-normalize=auto
```
log excerpt: 
```
kv_cache_lookup key=sha256:8f3a1... result=miss reason=key_mismatch input_norm=tokenized_v2 canonical_form="the quick brown" vs_canonical_form="the quick brown\u0000"
kv_cache_insert key=sha256:8f3a1... inserted
kv_cache_lookup key=sha256:5b2c9... result=miss reason=hash-diff input_norm=tokenized_v1 canonical_form="The Quick Brown" vs_canonical_form="the quick brown"
```

miguel: That log smells like a normalization/canonicalization regression — tiling_v2 changed how trailing padding / nulls are emitted into prefix bytes, and our key hashing doesn't strip them reliably. If kernel introduced a new tokenization post-processing (lowercasing + pad-trim), keys will diverge.

sam: Could also be that fused-attn kernels reorder buffers (packed vs unpacked) and our prefix serializer depends on memory layout. Did the runtime switch to the fast path that bypasses the legacy serializer?

perf-bot: profile uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/profiles/4123456789/hybrid-attn-qty8-flame.svg (10.2MB). Summary: increased time in kv_lookup path due to repeated hash recomputation, 23% more CPU on serializer.

jia: Steps to reproduce locally? We should repro on small prompt set and compare raw bytes going into sha256. If keys differ before hash, we know it's canonicalization. I'll run a diff harness against the old and new kernels.

erin: Repro script (quick):
```
# run with old and new runtime builds
python tools/repro_prefix_key_diff.py --model rbig --prompt-file tests/prefixes/sample_50.txt --kernel old > old_keys.json
python tools/repro_prefix_key_diff.py --model rbig --prompt-file tests/prefixes/sample_50.txt --kernel new > new_keys.json
jq -S . old_keys.json > a && jq -S . new_keys.json > b && git diff --no-index a b | head
```
The script logs "raw_prefix_bytes" and the computed sha256 for each request.

miguel: I ran a few locally and confirm: new kernel emits an extra 0x00 at end of canonicalized prefix for ~37% of prompts with certain trailing punctuation. So keys shift. Short-term mitigation: canonicalize by trimming trailing 0x00 before hashing in the prefix path. It's a tiny patch and low-risk.

sam: Are there side effects? Trimming could make two distinct prefixes collide if padding was meaningful for some model? I think padding should never be part of the key — we expect canonicalization to remove it. But let's add a unit test that asserts no collision for intentionally distinct inputs.

erin: Plan: (1) hotfix to prefix serializer: strip trailing nulls and normalize case/whitespace before hashing (PR in 15m), (2) rollout to canary pool + perf smoke (validate hit-rate returns), (3) add regression test to e2e harness.

perf-bot: Canary rollout started for canary hosts: canary-rt-3, canary-rt-7. Will post metrics in 10m.

jia: Also add a small metric: prefix_key_version and kernel_build_id tags to KV metrics so future kernel swaps are auditable.

erin: Agreed. Also adding an alert: prefix_hit_delta > 20% within 30m after a kernel change.

miguel: FYI — I'll open a follow-up to look at whether quant profile aq8_dynamic changed rounding in the tokenizer encoder path; possible secondary cause.

sam: Sounds good. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

erin: Update 20m: canary hit-rate back to ~58% on canary hosts after hotfix. Scheduling gradual rollout.
